author: Pallas, 1773
summary: 해마다 10건이 채 안 되게 기록되는 길잃은새로, 12월부터 이듬해 3월 사이 하천이나 저수지에서 드물게 보인다. 주로 물풀을 먹으며, 잠수도 하지만 다른 흰죽지류보다 얕은 물에서 물구나무서듯 먹이를 찾는 일이 많다. 유럽 남부에서 중앙아시아와 몽골에 걸쳐 번식하고, 인도 아대륙과 아프리카 북부 등지에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: dark brown cap over pale whitish cheeks (female)
broad white wing-bar along the flight feathers

sexes.male: 둥글게 부푼 머리는 주황빛 적갈색이고 부리는 산호빛 붉은색이다. 목과 가슴, 꼬리 쪽은 검고 옆구리는 희며 등은 갈색이다.
sexes.female: 몸은 옅은 갈색이고 정수리부터 뒷목까지 짙은 갈색이며 뺨과 멱은 희끄무레하다. 부리는 어두운 색에 끝이 분홍빛이다.

young: 어린새는 암컷과 매우 비슷하나 부리가 어두운 회색이고 눈은 옅은 갈색이다. 어린 수컷은 곧 머리깃이 부풀고 부리와 눈에 붉은 기가 돌기 시작한다.

art.subject: Red-crested Pochard (Netta rufina), adult male in winter, as seen in Korea from November to March: large bushy head bright rusty-orange, paler golden-orange on the raised crown; neck, breast and a broad band at the front of the body black; back and folded wings grey-brown; flanks clean white; a white patch at the bend of the wing showing at the front of the back; rump, vent and undertail coverts black; bill bright coral-red with a pale nail; red iris; legs orange-red.
art.pose: swimming on calm open water, side view, head held high
art.scene: Korean reservoir in winter with calm open water and dry reeds along the shore; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male in winter, side view swimming with the head held high: large rounded rusty-orange head, bright red bill, red iris, black neck and breast, brown back, white flanks, black tail and undertail
adult female, side view swimming: pale brown body with a darker back, dark brown cap reaching down to eye level, whitish-grey cheeks and throat, greyish bill with a pinkish patch near the tip

adult male in flight seen squarely from above: head, body and tail in one line, wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, broad white wing-bar along almost the whole length of the flight feathers, brown back, black breast and tail, orange head
art.build: Large, bulky diving duck, about the size of a Mallard, with a big rounded head that looks puffed up on the crown and a thick neck. Bill straight, fairly narrow, a little shorter than the head. Legs short, set well back. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail base. Tail short, dark. Floats high for a diving duck. In flight a broad white wing-bar along almost the whole length of the flight feathers and whitish underwings; males show white shoulder patches.
avoid: Do not paint a grey body, a dark bill and a dull chestnut head; that is Common Pochard (Aythya ferina).
Do not paint a flat, sleek crown; the male's head is large and fluffy.
Do not give the male pale cheeks; pale grey-white cheeks under a dark brown cap belong to the brown female.
Do not paint a dark or yellow bill on the male; it is bright red.
